analysis.session_summary: The tape was dominated by a NZD CPI miss: quarterly CPI printed 0.7% vs 0.8% forecast, sending NZD down 0.124% and making it the weakest major at -0.403%. JPY was the strongest, up 0.627%, with USD/JPY -116.2 pips and closing near the low at 0.14 of range, despite no Japanese releases. US unemployment claims beat at 194K vs 200K but the USD basket moved only 0.019%, inside the noise floor, and USD gains were rejected at -0.111%. Geopolitical Gulf headlines lifted VIX 4.837% and hit EM FX, but did not own any major leg.

themes.evidence: JPY strength 0.627%, USD/JPY -116.2 pips and close in 0.14 of range; CHF/JPY -81.0 pips.
NZD CPI actual 0.7% vs forecast 0.8%; NZD -0.403%; NZD/USD -16.4 pips; AUD/NZD +19.0 pips.
Unemployment Claims actual 194K vs 200K, basket moved 0.019%; USD -0.111%, attempt rejected 78%.

currency_drivers.EUR: Attempted early gain reversed 77%; no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.JPY: Broad safe-haven bid; sold early then recovered 79%, no own releases.
currency_drivers.GBP: Held its range, no own releases, no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.AUD: Held its range with no own releases and no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.CAD: Held its range, no own releases, no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.CHF: Held its range, no own releases, no clear catalyst.
currency_drivers.NZD: CPI miss printed 0.7% vs 0.8%, weaker 0.124%; rally gave back 83%.

leg_notes.EUR/USD: EUR/USD traded in a four-leg chop: early dip -13.8 pips, Asia rebound +32.4, NY-morning selloff -62.3, late bounce +33.0; no leg had a clear catalyst.

polarity_reads.read: Normal miss reaction: NZD weakened 0.124% on a 0.7% vs 0.8% print, so the currency moved in the direction of the surprise without a contrarian fade.
Muted reaction with USD basket at 0.019% inside noise floor implies the better print was already priced or was not a positioning trigger.

scenarios.name: Base: range retention, residual JPY bid
scenarios.thesis: Momentum from the NZD CPI shock fades; G10 pairs hold today's ranges with no new catalyst, and JPY strength eases from peak but USD/JPY stays heavy.
scenarios.invalidation: A sustained break above 156.914 in USD/JPY or VIX above 19.085 revives USD.

pair_paths.rationale: Today's 66.9-pip range likely contains EUR/USD absent a catalyst.
USD/JPY fell 116.2 pips today; residual JPY bid can repeat that scale.
NZD/USD fell 16.4 pips on the CPI miss and closed low in range.

scenarios.name: Risk-off Gulf escalation
scenarios.thesis: Gulf headlines turn from noise to driver: safe-haven JPY and CHF bid while high-beta and EM currencies sell.
triggers: State Dept ordered departure headlines intensify

pair_paths.rationale: Safe-haven JPY bid; today's USD/JPY drop of 116.2 pips can extend.
CHF strength; today's USD/CHF fell 25.8 pips.
EM risk-off; today's USD/MXN rose 915.9 pips.

scenarios.name: Data-driven PMI/UoM repricing
scenarios.thesis: Flash PMIs and UoM surprises force EUR and GBP to take out today's ranges; any US data disappointment strengthens the case for lower USD.
triggers: Euro area flash PMIs beat 50.5 and 53.5
scenarios.invalidation: PMIs and UoM all print in line, leaving ranges intact.

pair_paths.rationale: EUR/USD range is 66.9 pips; a positive PMI shock can produce a full-range move.
GBP/USD range is 63.9 pips; UK PMIs could drive a full-range up day.
USD/JPY range is 165.3 pips; cross-currents keep it contained.

risks.why_it_matters: VIX/USD rose 4.837% and EM FX weakened; headline risk can flip risk sentiment quickly.
NZD is weakest at -0.403% and NZD/USD close at 0.38 of range; a bounce in NZD/USD can unwind crosses.
USD attempt rejected and DXY -8.2 points; a better data calendar could force a short-covering bounce.
Flash PMIs can shift rate expectations after a day with no clear catalysts.

analysis.calendar_ahead_note: UK Retail Sales m/m (-0.1% fcst), French/German flash PMIs, US flash PMIs (55.4 mfg, 57.9 svc), and revised UoM 46.3 can change the picture; PMI surprises are the key.
